- Model consistently underestimates price spikes in the 10–15 day horizon, especially after low points; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for such periods.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., 77.73 → 80.03) and fails to correct downward quickly; apply a “cool-down” bias to prevent overcorrection.
- Mean reversion is overestimated in early horizon (1–3 days); reduce forecast slope for short-term corrections.
- Sentiment history is flat (all 0.00) — no behavioral signal — so ignore sentiment-driven adjustments; rely solely on price momentum and volatility clustering.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are too conservative in the first 5–7 days; increase initial forecast by 3–8% to capture early momentum.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in 3 consecutive days, apply a “rebound bias” to next forecast — anticipate continued upward trend.
- If forecast is below true outcome by >10% for 3+ days, apply “lag correction” — add 1–2% per day to catch delayed rebound.
